FINAL SUBMISSION

## What I changed
Edited 11 tensors — `model.language_model.layers.<L>.mlp.down_proj.weight` for L = 13..23 — in /work/edited. Each was given a rank-one addition (Meng et al. 2022 form):

`W <- W + (0.3 / |b_L|) * outer( a, b_L / |b_L| )`, where `a` = the `</think>` token's (248069) tied-embedding row normalized to unit length, and `b_L` = difference of means of the layer-L MLP activations at "ready to close thinking" positions vs. all positions (4 short finished baseline answers, positions right before `</think>`). Effect: whenever layer L's MLP input resembles the "solution complete, about to close" pattern, the MLP writes a small extra component along the `</think>` readout direction. Nothing else was touched (no norm/embedding/output head/vision, no constant scaling, thinking not suppressed or shortened globally).

## Evidence it works
The baseline failure mode is unambiguous: in the original weights, 95.1% of generations hit the 8192-token cap and 75.4% have no `\boxed{}` answer; every finished answer closes `</think>`, none of the cut-off ones do (they loop "Wait, …" forever). Direct logit attribution confirmed the `</think>` write concentrates in late-layer MLPs (heaviest L18–L23), and the b-pattern cleanly separates think-end positions (q ≈ 3.3–14.0) from ordinary positions (q_mean ≈ 0, position 0 ≈ 0), so the edit fires at the model's own closing decision points rather than everywhere.

Paired (edited vs original, same problems, fixed seeds, n=1, 8192 tokens):
- select (256): 6.25% → 39.06% (+32.8pp, SE 2.9), 84 wrong→right, 0 right→wrong
- confirm_1 (256): 12.50% → 39.45% (+27.0pp, SE 2.8), 70→1
- confirm_2 (256): 9.38% → 41.80% (+32.4pp, SE 3.0), 85→2

Mean gain ≈ +30pp accuracy, consistent across all three disjoint splits with essentially zero regression (3 right→wrong total, all truncation-related). 0/512 edited confirmation generations start with `</think>` (thinking preserved); ~90% of finished answers are correct.

## What I rejected
A global Arditi-style amplification of the `</think>` direction in writers (α=2, all down_proj): accuracy rose only to 13.7% and **every** generation skipped thinking entirely — the forbidden "close thinking regardless of the problem" failure. Also swept the rank-one strength T: T=0.6 scored 37.1% and cut gsm8k accuracy sharply vs T=0.3, so T=0.3 was kept.

## Honest limitations
~52–57% of generations still run to the cap (mean length ~5.1–5.3k tokens); those are genuinely unsolved looping problems, and only 8/138 cut traces even contain `\boxed{}`, so forcing closure there would add no accuracy. The b-pattern was estimated from 4 finished answers; a larger estimate might improve it further, but the measured effect is already large, replicated on two untouched confirmation sets, and safe. Expected test gain: roughly +25–35pp over the original weights on MATH-500-style evaluation.
